_note: Manual WCAG 2.1 A and AA checks for decidiq, filled in per release by a tester (platform-accessibility-audit-report, plt-22). result is pass, fail, not-applicable or not-tested; an empty result counts as not-tested, never as pass. Record the tester and the date with every result.

entries.check: Every image, icon button and chart has a text alternative that says what it shows or does.
Every prerecorded audio-only or video-only item, such as a meeting recording without sound, has a transcript or a text alternative.
Every prerecorded video with sound, such as a meeting recording, has captions.
Every prerecorded video has an audio description or a full text alternative.
Headings, lists, tables and form labels are marked up as such, so a screen reader announces the same structure you see.
Read each page with a screen reader: the reading order matches the visual order.
No instruction relies only on shape, colour, size, position or sound, such as "click the green button on the right".
Colour is never the only way to tell things apart, such as a vote result or a status badge.
Audio that plays by itself for more than three seconds can be paused or muted.
Every function works with the keyboard alone: open a meeting, cast a vote, reorder the agenda, fill in a form.
Tab into and out of every dialog, menu and editor without getting stuck.
Any single-key shortcut can be turned off or remapped, or only works while its component has focus.
Every time limit, such as a voting round or a session timeout, can be turned off, adjusted or extended.
Moving, blinking or auto-updating content, such as a live agenda or a timer, can be paused, stopped or hidden.
Nothing flashes more than three times in one second.
A skip link or landmarks let you jump past the navigation to the main content.
Tab through each page: focus moves in an order that keeps the meaning, and a closed dialog returns focus to what opened it.
Every link says where it goes, alone or with its sentence, list item or table cell.
Everything done with a multipoint or path gesture, such as drag to reorder, can also be done with a single tap or click.
An action fires on release, not on press, or can be cancelled by moving away.
The accessible name of each control contains its visible label text.
Nothing works only by shaking or tilting the device.
Focusing a control never submits a form, opens a window or moves you elsewhere.
Changing a field or a choice never submits or navigates without warning.
A form error names the field and says what is wrong, in text.
Every form field has a visible label or instruction.
Every control, including custom ones like the vote buttons and the agenda reorder, exposes its name, role and state to a screen reader.
A live meeting stream offered with sound has live captions.
Every prerecorded video has an audio description where the picture carries information the sound does not.
Every page works in portrait and in landscape.
Fields asking for the user's own details, such as name and email, carry the matching autocomplete value.
At 200 percent browser zoom all text is readable and no function is lost.
No text is shown as an image, apart from logos.
At 320 CSS pixels wide (400 percent zoom) each page reads without scrolling in two directions, apart from tables and the agenda grid.
Borders of fields and buttons, focus rings, icons and chart parts have a contrast of at least 3 to 1.
With increased line, paragraph, letter and word spacing no text is cut off or overlaps.
A tooltip or popover can be dismissed with Escape, can be hovered, and stays until you move away.
Each page can be reached in more than one way, such as the navigation and the search.
Headings and labels say what the section or field is about.
The keyboard focus is always visible.
Text in another language than the page, such as a Dutch motion title on an English page, is marked with its language where it matters.
The navigation appears in the same place and order on every page.
Controls with the same function, such as Save or Delete, have the same name everywhere.
When a correction is known, such as a date format, the error message suggests it.
A vote, a signature or a deletion can be reviewed, corrected or confirmed before it is final.
A saved, queued or failed message is announced by a screen reader without moving focus.
